title: Help Wanted: One Friendly Digger
text:
Help wanted! The Maple Street building site needs a friendly digger. We are building a new playground, and we need someone who can dig {adverb} and work well with others. Our last digger {past tense verb} away to join the circus.

The right digger must have a strong scoop, a {adjective} horn, and at least {number} {plural noun}. You must be able to lift dirt, move rocks, and {verb} without making a mess. Diggers who can tell jokes about {plural noun} get extra points.

Every Friday, each digger gets a {adjective} car wash and a snack of {food}. You will share a parking spot with a dump truck named Gus. Gus is very nice, but he likes {verb ending in ing} at six in the morning.

To apply, roll over to the trailer, honk twice, and say "{exclamation}!" Tell us why you are the most {adjective} digger in town, and please bring a {noun} for the break room.

title: Good Morning from Foreman Rosa
text:
Good morning, team! This is Foreman Rosa on the big loudspeaker. Please put down your coffee and listen up.

Today we are pouring the floor for the new fire station. The cement truck will arrive at nine o'clock with {number} loads of cement and one load of {plural noun}. Please stay {adverb} out of the way while it backs up. It beeps like a {adjective} {animal}.

A few reminders. Hard hats must be worn at all times, even during lunch. Please do not {verb} on the fresh cement, and please stop drawing {plural noun} in it with sticks. Yesterday someone left a {noun} in the tool shed, and it is still {verb ending in ing}.

One more thing. Today is Big Mike's birthday! At lunch we will sing to him by the crane while hopping on one {body part}. His cake is shaped like a {noun}. Thank you, team, and have a {adjective} day.

title: Plans for Our Brand New Library
text:
These are the official building plans for the new Oak Hill Library. The town has saved money for {number} years, so we want it to be perfect.

The front door will be painted bright {color} and will be big enough for a {animal} to walk through. In the lobby, a fountain will spray {plural noun} every hour on the hour.

The kids' room will have bean bags, a {adjective} reading tent, and a slide shaped like a giant {noun}. Children may {verb} quietly during story time. The second floor is for grown-ups who like to read {adverb}. A sign by the desk will say: No running, no shouting, and no {verb ending in ing}.

The roof will have a garden full of {adjective} flowers and {plural noun}. On opening day, the mayor will cut the ribbon and read everyone a {adjective} book about {plural noun}.

title: Visitor Rules at the Building Site
text:
Welcome to the Pine Street building site! We are building a new pet store with a {noun} on the roof. Please read these rules {adverb}.

All visitors must stay behind the orange fence. You may wave at the workers, but please do not ask them to {verb}. Every visitor gets a hard hat and a vest that smells a little bit like {plural noun}. Please give them back when you leave, even if they look {adjective} on you.

You may take pictures of the crane and the big pile of {plural noun}. Our bulldozer, Daisy, gets shy if you stare at her {adverb}. Last week, a visitor {past tense verb} at her, and she hid for an hour. The crane driver, Mr. Lopez, likes to wave with his {body part}.

The snack table has juice boxes, {food}, and a {noun} for sharing. Foreman Jill can answer questions about bricks, cement, and {plural noun}. Come back next week to see the workers {verb ending in ing} on the roof!

title: The Lunch Truck Menu
text:
Every day at noon, the lunch truck parks next to the cement mixer and plays a song about {verb ending in ing}. Here is today's menu.

The Bulldozer Burger has lettuce, tomato, and a slice of {food} on top. It comes with a side of crunchy {plural noun}. The Crane Sandwich is so tall that you have to stand on a {noun} to take a bite. The Hard Hat Soup comes with a {noun} on the side and tastes very {adjective}.

For dessert, try our famous Brick Cake. It is chocolate on the outside and {color} on the inside. Our cook, Miss Bea, {past tense verb} for a whole week to invent it. Workers say it makes them want to {verb} all afternoon.

Please wait in line {adverb}, and do not feed your sandwich to the {animal} behind the fence. Today's special is a smoothie made with bananas, milk, and {plural noun}. Miss Bea says it will make your muscles feel {adjective}.

title: Diary of a Dump Truck Named Dot
text:
Dear Diary, my name is Dot, and I am a dump truck. I am big, I am yellow, and I am very {adjective}. Today was a busy day at the building site.

In the morning, the digger filled my back with dirt. Then it filled me with {adjective} rocks. Then, for some reason, it filled me with {number} {plural noun}. I drove them {adverb} to the other side of the site and dumped them in a neat pile.

At lunch, the workers sat in my shade and ate {food} sandwiches. A worker named Hank told a joke about a {noun}, and everyone {past tense verb}. Trucks laugh by honking, so I went "{sound}!"

This afternoon, I got muddy. Tomorrow is my bath day. The workers will scrub me with soap, a {noun}, and {plural noun} until I shine. Then I will {verb} all the way home to my garage and dream about {verb ending in ing}.

title: Week Three at the New School Building
text:
Hello, families! Here is our weekly update from the team building the new Willow Elementary School.

This week we finished the gym walls. The gym will be big enough to hold {number} {plural noun} at the same time. We also put in the big windows, and the workers cleaned them {adverb} until they sparkled.

On Wednesday, a {adjective} surprise arrived on a truck. It was the new playground slide! It is shaped like a {noun} and is very tall. Our crane, Big Bertha, lifted it into place while everybody {past tense verb}.

Next week, the painters will paint the hallways. The principal picked the color herself. It is called Sunny {silly word}. We will also start the lunchroom, where students will someday eat {food} and {verb} with their friends. The library will have {adjective} chairs and a shelf just for books about {plural noun}.

Thank you for being so patient while we keep {verb ending in ing}.

title: What Is Inside the Big Red Toolbox
text:
Uncle Ray is a builder, and he has a big red toolbox. Today he let me peek inside and write down everything I found.

The top drawer has a hammer, a {adjective} eraser, and a pencil that is only {number} inches long. It also has a little bag of {plural noun}. Uncle Ray uses them to fix {adjective} doors.

The middle drawer has screwdrivers in every size. The biggest one is as long as a {noun}. Next to them is a level with a bubble inside. When the bubble is in the middle, the shelf is straight. When the bubble starts {verb ending in ing}, you should {verb} and try again.

The bottom drawer has gloves, goggles, a {animal} sticker, and a very old granola bar that smells a little bit like {food}. Uncle Ray says a good builder always works {adverb} and never forgets his lucky {noun}. When I asked about the {plural noun} hidden in the corner, he just {past tense verb} and closed the drawer.

title: The View from the Crane Cab
text:
Dear Ellie, I am writing this letter from my crane. My little cab is way up high. It has a comfy seat, a {adjective} heater, and a picture of you {verb ending in ing}.

From up here, I can see the whole town. The cars look like tiny {plural noun}, and the river looks like a {adjective} ribbon. I can even see our house! Your dad is in the backyard. He just {past tense verb} with the dog.

Today I am lifting steel beams for the new hospital. I move them {adverb} and set them down gently. The workers on the ground talk to me on a radio. When things go well, they say "{exclamation}!" When they need me to stop, they say "{silly word}!"

At lunch, a {adjective} pigeon landed on my window and stared at my {food}. I named him Captain {noun}. When I get home tonight, let's {verb} together and eat {plural noun} for dessert. Love, Mom

title: The Grand Opening of the Bakery
text:
Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the grand opening of the Sweet Street Bakery! I am Mayor Gomez, and I am so happy to be here.

Six months ago, this was an empty lot with weeds and a {adjective} old fence. Then the builders came. They brought a bulldozer, a cement mixer, and {number} {plural noun}. They worked {adverb} every day, even when it was hot.

Now look at it! The bakery has a red roof, a big window, and an oven so large you could fit a {noun} inside. The baker, Mrs. Fig, says her first cake will taste like {food} and have {plural noun} on top.

The builders {past tense verb} when they saw it finished. Please give them a {adjective} cheer. Now it is time to cut the ribbon. When I do, I want everyone to {verb} and shout "{exclamation}!" Let the {verb ending in ing} begin!
